title: Complete the Architect to implementation round trip
summary: A user can import an Architect ProductSpec, place linked capabilities and screens on a Studio Board, propose visual/flow changes, hand an approved implementation package to Control/Codex, and reconcile the resulting code and screenshots against the original design.
acceptance_criteria: The journey starts from one explicit accepted `studio_workspace` artifact revision and identifies every intended consumer before any downstream change is proposed.
A human-readable preview shows the exact data fields, actions, visibility, sensitivity, freshness, expected effects, target repositories/apps, and permissions involved.
The user can accept all, accept selected scope, edit permitted local fields, defer, reject, or revoke; partial acceptance creates a derived handoff rather than mutating the source artifact.
The handoff uses a stable intent ID, source artifact ID/revision, target capability, requested action, idempotency key, expiry, approval/consent references, and expected receipt contract.
Studio shows which ProductSpec decisions and capabilities are represented, omitted, changed, or still unresolved.
The implementation handoff contains selected screens, component/constraint data, acceptance criteria, source targets, evidence requirements, and explicit non-scope.
Returned implementation evidence is compared three ways: original imported truth, approved Studio proposal, and implemented repository revision.
Divergence creates reviewable findings or ProductSpec amendments; Studio never silently declares code and design synchronized.
No consumer writes directly into another repository or application database; each target validates and imports through its own domain boundary and remains usable when the other app is absent.
Every accepted target returns a durable receipt with accepted fields/actions, rejected fields/actions, created/updated local IDs, warnings, source revision, target revision, and status.

Repeated delivery, retry after interruption, partial success, offline queuing, changed source revision, changed target capability, duplicate import, and conflicting local edits are deterministic and user-visible.
Update, supersession, correction, expiry, and revocation are explicit follow-up intents; a successful earlier handoff is never silently rewritten.
The UI represents unavailable, waiting-for-consent, queued, delivered, partially accepted, rejected, conflicted, revoked, and stale states distinctly and never colors unavailable as success.

The entire journey supports keyboard/navigation accessibility, Dynamic Type or platform-equivalent scaling, Czech/English copy where the app supports those locales, and reduced-motion behavior where relevant.

Telemetry is minimal and privacy-preserving: it records coarse journey state and failure class, not payload contents, personal identifiers, secrets, raw paths, full URLs, or health/family/customer narrative.
Deterministic producer/consumer fixtures and end-to-end tests cover normal, stale, offline, duplicate, partial, conflict, rejection, revocation, and recovery paths.
The strongest repository-native tests, builds, contract checks, artifact conformance, UI/runtime evidence, and diff gates pass with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Convergence Wave 3; explicit cross-application user journey ticket.
Estimated effort: XL, approximately 7-14 focused working days after producer and protocol prerequisites.
Implementation risk: high because the slice crosses product, privacy, compatibility, offline, and ownership boundaries.

User outcome: A user can import an Architect ProductSpec, place linked capabilities and screens on a Studio Board, propose visual/flow changes, hand an approved implementation package to Control/Codex, and reconcile the resulting code and screenshots against the original design.
External portfolio prerequisites: mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0163, mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0164, mrPoky/HumbleControl#HC-0165, mrPoky/HumbleArchitect#HA-0012, mrPoky/HumbleWebsite#HWE-0093.
Non-scope: do not add background auto-import, silent cross-app mutation, cloud accounts, shared global databases, or implicit consent.

Alternative considered and rejected: provide only an Open-in-app deep link — a deep link cannot express data minimization, partial acceptance, idempotency, offline recovery, receipts, revocation, or conflict handling.
Ship one narrow end-to-end fixture and receipt loop before adding more consumers or broader automation.

Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain-conditional; priority band later. Optional platform interoperability remains useful, but independent product quality now takes precedence and no merger is implied.
Wave 10 final rationalization: consolidate-into-fusion-program; portfolio band later. Keep only as input to the reversible platform fusion program.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `optional-reference-or-research`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-optional`, relevance `later`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `proven product need and explicit consented boundary`. Cross-application work remains conditional and must not displace standalone product quality or the game completion gates.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-platform-reference` / `later` / priority `medium`. Cross-app work is valid only when a validated user or operator need exists.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-research-or-reference`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `later`. Cross-app work is valid only when a validated user or operator need exists.
